column1: # Each of Bevy's examples and what this engine makes of it, read by build/examples-table.py.
# A line is a name, a state and a note, apart by tabs. The state is can (everything it uses is
# bridged and nobody has written it yet), missing (the note names what the bridge lacks) or n/a
# (the note says why it is not a thing a C# game does). One of Bevy's components the bridge
# reaches through reflection (EcsWorld.InsertReflected and its kin) counts as bridged, and the
# note names it. An example written here is found by its file under BevyCSharp.Examples. Its line
# is can with a note saying how it differs from Bevy's in no feature, or part with a note naming
# the feature of Bevy's it leaves out.
